{{short description|Colombian ornithologist}}
'''Álvaro José Negret''' (1949 – July 18, 1998) was a Colombian scientist and author specializing in [[ornithology]] and [[Conservation (ethic)|conservation]]. Negret as a boy collected birds for the Natural History Museum of the [[University of Cauca]] in [[Popayán]]. As an [[undergraduate]] Negret co-founded the Natural History Museum at the [[University of Caldas]] before completing a [[Master's degree]] in Ecology and Management of Natural Resources at the [[University of Brasília]] in [[Brazil]].<ref name=eponym>{{cite book |last1=Beolens |first=Bo |last2=Watkins |first2=Michael |last3=Grayson |first3=Michael |date=2014 |title=The Eponym Dictionary of Birds |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=En4wBAAAQBAJ&pg=PT917 |location=Bedford Square, London |publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing Plc |page=917 |isbn=9781472905734 |access-date=2015-01-10 }}</ref> Upon his return to Colombia Negret became a professor at the [[University of Cauca]] and Director of its Natural History Museum from 1987–98.<ref name=cotinga>{{cite journal |url=http://www.ambiotek.com/herb/alvaro.htm |title=Alvaro Jose Negret ~ 1949-1998 |last1=Salaman |first1=Paul |date= |publisher=Ambiotek |journal=[[Cotinga (journal)|Cotinga]] |access-date=2015-01-12}}</ref> He was married to [[geologist]] Patricia Torres.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=es&u=http://museo.unicauca.edu.co/&prev=search |title=History |last1= |first1= |last2= |first2= |date= |website=[[University of Cauca]] |publisher=[[Google Translate]] |access-date=2015-01-12}}</ref>

As a conservationist, Negret helped found and manage the Tambito Nature Reserve which contains over 300 bird [[species]]. He also worked in coordination with [[Conservation International]] to design the Naya Corridor Program and unify two national parks ([[Farallones de Cali]] and [[Munchique]]), creating a massive conservation zone for protection of wildlife.<ref name=cotinga/> At the time of his death he was working on a book about Colombia's endangered bird species entitled ''Aves Colombianas Amenazadas de Extinción'' (Engl. ''Threatened Birds of Colombia'').<ref name=eponym/>

==Legacy==

The HERB Project (Hydrology Ecology and Regional Biodiversity) in Colombia, described as "a collaborative programme between the Department of Geography, [[King's College London]], [[UK]], the Universidad del Cauca, the [[Alexander von Humboldt Biological Resources Research Institute|Instituto de Investigacion de Recursos Biologicos]], Alexander Von Humboldt of the [[Ministry of Environment (Colombia)|Colombian Ministry of Environment]], [[International Center for Tropical Agriculture|CIAT]] and a number of other research groups in Colombia," is dedicated to the memory of Álvaro José Negret and continues his work on conservation.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ambiotek.com/herb/herb.htm |title=The HERB Project (Hydrology Ecology and Regional Biodiversity) |last1= |first1= |last2= |first2= |date=1999 |website=Ambiotek.com |publisher= |access-date=2015-01-12}}</ref>

The [[Munchique wood wren]] (''henicorhina negreti'') is named in Álvaro José Negret's honor.<ref>{{cite book |last=Woods |first=Sarah |date=2012 |title=Bradt Colombia |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-xoZwlNgYGAC&pg=PA13 |location=[[Guilford, Connecticut]] |publisher=The Globe Pequot Press |page=13 |isbn=9781841623641 |access-date=2015-01-10 }}</ref> Negret is also honored in the 2011 book, ''Tropical Montane Cloud Forests: Science for Conservation and Management'', for allowing research at Tambito.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bruijnzeel |first1=L.A. |last2=Scatena |first2=F.N. |last3=Hamilton |first3=S. |date=2010 |title=Tropical Montane Cloud Forests: Science for Conservation and Management |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=N6FkwMnSX8EC&pg=PA523 |location=[[Cambridge]], [[New York (state)|NY]] |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |pages=259, 523 |isbn=9780521760355 |access-date=2015-01-10 }}</ref> The University of Cauca has named its Botanical Garden after him.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=es&u=http://www.periodicolacampana.com/se-diluyo-el-sueno-de-caldas-de-fernandez-perez-y-de-negret-fernandez/&prev=search |title=Se diluyó el sueño de Caldas, de Fernández Pérez y de Negret Fernández |last1=Olano |first1=Aura Isabel |date=2014-12-27 |website=Periódico La Campana |publisher=[[Google Translate]] |access-date=2015-01-12}}</ref>

His son [https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=DiWp0CAAAAAJ&hl=en Pablo Jose Negret], has followed his footsteps doing research in ecology and conservation of tropical forest.
